spots.name: Lotus Tower
spots.label: Lotus Tower

text.geographic_location: The Lotus Tower is in Colombo 01, on the waterfront of Beira Lake, alongside D. R. Wijewardene Mawatha.
text.access_note: The area around the tower is a waterfront, but please check current access details before you go.
text.description: The Lotus Tower, also called the Colombo Lotus Tower, is a slender, lotus-shaped tower beside Beira Lake. It stands 351.5 metres tall, and as of 2019 it was the tallest self-supported structure in South Asia. The design takes its shape from the lotus flower, which in Sri Lankan culture stands for purity, and the base echoes a lotus throne. That simple, recognisable outline is what makes it work so well in a photo: one tall shape against the sky, with the lake and city around it. Its lights can change colour, so an evening visit can give you a very different picture from a daytime one. Work was under way from January 2012, and the opening ceremony was held on 16 September 2019. The tower carries broadcasting antennas and also has visitor facilities, including an observation gallery. The phone icon on the map sits at the middle of the tower, within or beside its base area, so you will be near its base, looking up. For the full shape, walk back a little along the waterfront until the whole tower fits in the frame. Keep the phone upright and level so the sides stay straight. Try one wide shot with the lake or some foreground, and one close shot of the textured base. People walking past can give a useful sense of scale.
text.directions_text: Start from Colombo 01, the area around Beira Lake, and head to the tower. The Lotus Tower (Colombo Lotus Tower) is on the Beira Lake waterfront in Colombo 01. The phone icon on the map is at the middle of the tower, so once you reach the tower's base area you are in the right place. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Late afternoon into dusk is a good choice, as the light softens and the tower's colour-changing lights can be seen against the darkening sky.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and line the tower up with a vertical line so it does not lean. Point the phone straight ahead rather than tilting it far upwards, then step back to get the top in. Use the lake or some paving as a foreground to add depth. For a bolder shot, hold the phone low and shoot the base against the sky with the ultra-wide.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x), because from close to the tower's base it is the only lens that fits much of the height into the frame. Use the default lens (1x) for tidier, less stretched shots once you step back. If your phone has a telephoto (2x-5x), use it from a distance to pick out the top of the tower.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. For a full-height view, walk back along the waterfront until the whole tower fits in the frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the tower to focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little so the sky does not turn white. After dark, use night mode and brace your elbows against your body to keep the lights sharp.

spots.alt: Lotus Tower, Colombo: a slender, lotus-shaped tower beside Beira Lake. Photo spot

spots.name: Pettah Market
spots.label: Pettah Market

text.geographic_location: In the Pettah district of Colombo, at the market entrance marked by the Khan Clock Tower on a roundabout. The market lies beyond the entrance.
text.access_note: According to one guide, Sunday retail is reduced and wholesale is closed, so expect a quieter market on that day.
text.description: Pettah Market, also known as Manning Market, is an open market in the Pettah district of Colombo. Its entrance is marked by the Khan Clock Tower, a tall monument standing in the middle of a roundabout. The tower was built by the family of Framjee Bhickajee Khan, a well-known Parsi family from Bombay who had large business interests in Sri Lanka and owned the Colombo Oil Mills. For a phone photographer it is a good place to begin. The tower gives you a clear upright subject, and the market entrance and the movement of people sit below it, so a single frame says 'this is where the market starts'. Stand across the street from the tower and fit both the tower and the crowd at its base into the picture. Once you have that shot, walk into the market for closer pictures. Inside, the open-air aisles have produce and goods with workers moving through, and Keyzer Street has older stalls with colourful displays arranged by type of goods. Ask before you photograph any vendor. According to one guide, Sunday retail is reduced and wholesale is closed, so weekdays or Saturday mornings give you the busiest scenes. Some maps may use a different name for the tower, so look for the roundabout.
text.directions_text: No station or tram stop is listed for this spot, so use a map app to reach the Khan Clock Tower in the Pettah area. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Weekdays or Saturday mornings, when the market is busiest. Sunday is much quieter.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on the gridlines and put the tower on one vertical line with the entrance and street activity along the bottom. Keep your phone upright so the full height of the tower fits. For a second view, walk into the market for open aisles of produce, or to Keyzer Street for older stalls and vendors.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) from across the street so the whole tower and the crowd below it fit in. Switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x) if traffic or people stop you stepping back. Use telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for the clock face and stall details.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject (across the street from the tower, framing the market entrance below it). The four-storey clock tower with the market entrance and street activity beneath it, a clear marker for where the market begins. The best place to stand is across the street from the Khan Clock Tower at the market entrance, so the entrance is framed below the tower. Check the tower's exact position on the map when you arrive.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the people or stalls to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly so the sky behind the tower does not wash out. Hold the shutter for a Live Photo to catch the street moving. Ask before photographing vendors.

spots.alt: Pettah Market, Colombo: an open market in the Pettah district of Colombo. Photo spot

spots.name: Galle Face Hotel
spots.label: Galle Face Hotel

text.geographic_location: The hotel is on Galle Road in Colombo, facing the long seafront lawn of Galle Face Green, with the Indian Ocean just beyond.
text.access_note: Galle Face Green is a public open space, but the hotel itself is private property, so take your photos from the green and check the official site before you go if you plan to visit the hotel's restaurants or museum.
text.description:
The Galle Face Hotel is a long, colonial-era seafront building on Galle Road, and it is one of the oldest hotels east of Suez. It was founded in 1864 by four British entrepreneurs and began as a Dutch villa called Galle Face House. It takes its name from Galle Face Green, the stretch of lawn it faces. The south wing, designed by the architect Edward Skinner, was completed in 1894. The property has stayed largely unchanged since then, apart from careful restorations, including a refurbishment of the north wing that finished in 2015.

It photographs well because of the setting. The old facade sits right beside the open lawn and the Indian Ocean, so one frame can hold history, grass, sky and sea. The best place for this is the northern end of Galle Face Green, where the promenade begins beside the hotel. From there the hotel's colonial front fills one side of the frame, with the ocean and the sea-facing lawn behind or beside it. It looks best as the light softens in the late afternoon.

Stay on the public green rather than going into the hotel grounds, as the hotel is private property. If you want a plain sunset over the water, walk further along the green. The hotel is not part of that view, but the open horizon, often with ships on it, is a good second shot. Leave a little sky above the roofline so the building has room.
text.directions_text: The hotel is directly south of that point, about 1 minute on foot. Head for the green rather than the hotel entrance. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Late afternoon, roughly 4 to 5 pm, when the light is softer and you can find a spot before the crowds build.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and line the horizon up with one of the horizontal lines so the sea sits level. Place the hotel on one side of the frame and let the lawn lead the eye towards it. Leave a little sky above the roofline. If the facade is too wide to fit, try panorama mode, moving slowly and keeping the phone level.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) to fit the long facade and the sea in one frame. Switch to the default lens (1x) for a calmer, more natural view, and use telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for details of the building.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand in Galle Face Green (northern end, where the promenade begins beside the hotel). The hotel's colonial facade in the frame, with the ocean and the sea-facing lawn behind or beside it. The hotel lies to the south. From here you see its colonial facade in the frame, with the ocean and the sea-facing lawn behind or beside it. If you want an open sunset instead, with no hotel in the picture, walk further along the green; that view shows the Indian Ocean and often ships on the horizon.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the hotel facade to focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little if the sky is washing out. Taking a few frames in quick succession helps when people walk through the shot.

spots.alt: Galle Face Hotel, Colombo: a long, colonial-era seafront building on Galle Road. Photo spot
